inputs.share_count_basis: 26,590.7m shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim report) plus 822m H shares from assumed full conversion of the USD1,999.8m 2024 H-share convertible bonds (conversion price HK$18.97, deep in the money against the quote at inputs.price_as_of; 7.80 HKD/USD) plus ~50m options/restricted shares/ESOP (FY2025 note 69 dilutive table). The USD1.5bn 2026 zero-coupon CB (conversion HK$62.65) is out of the money and left in debt. Count held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: H1 FY2026 balance sheet (30 June 2026): borrowings + bonds + current portions + lease liabilities + other current liabilities = RMB165,632m (CSV TotalDebt) less cash and bank balances RMB91,318m = RMB74,314m; less RMB14,300m carrying value of the 2024 H-share CB (USD1,999.8m at ~7.15 CNY/USD) which is treated as converted (its 822m shares are in the diluted count) = RMB60,014m. Gold-lease liabilities are left out (matched by gold inventory). Lease liabilities (RMB278m incl. current) are immaterial and sit inside debt (treatment A).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income RMB2,616m is NOT stripped: the company is a net debtor (net debt RMB60-74bn), so there is no cash pile being added to EV. The forward EBITDA path is built from core operating profit before finance costs, so interest income is outside the flows anyway.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow note 71 'Share-based payment cost' RMB225,989,411 (file 2899.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:18615); no separate equity-award tax line disclosed (CAS filer, SBC ~0.07% of revenue)
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 A-share repurchases RMB1,000m; H1 FY2026 RMB2,500m. Buybacks fund the flat count; SBC is immaterial so this is essentially a capital return.
inputs.fx_note: CNY/HKD 1.1746 HKD per CNY (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-22T06:46Z; inverse HKDCNY=X 0.8505). Statements and all flows are RMB (CAS, same for A and H shares); the HKEX quote is HKD. Per-share values are computed in CNY and multiplied by 1.1746 for the HKD canonical fields. Parity check against the A-share dual listing: 601899.SS CNY27.76 x 1.1746 = HK$32.61 A-share-implied value, against which the H share (current_price at inputs.price_as_of) trades at a ~10% discount, the normal A/H premium range -- direction and quote basis confirmed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10y China Government Bond ~1.8%, China ERP ~6.0%, beta 1.2 gives ~9.0% cost of equity; +1.5pp jurisdiction premium for the DRC/Serbia/Central Asia/PNG asset base (country risk is not modelled in the scenarios, so it is charged here, once) = 10.5%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.8% (CNY bonds 2.5-3.5%, USD CBs 0-1%); market-value weights ~80/20 equity/debt (market cap ~RMB660bn vs gross debt RMB165bn) = 9.0% WACC. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- commodity-price risk is in the flows, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: A: leases as debt. Lease liabilities (RMB278m incl. current) are inside total_debt; right-of-use depreciation (RMB212m FY2025) sits inside the D&A line; no lease charge in EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE in the flows, not in the bridge. Non-controlling interests took 18.7% of FY2025 net profit (RMB11,893m of 63,822m) and 20.1% of H1 FY2026 (RMB10,643m... reported 9,881m to NCI of 49,813m total per the P&L face incl. other items); cash dividends to minorities were RMB5,139m FY2025 and RMB6,305m H1 FY2026. NCI book value (RMB67,221m at 30 June 2026) badly understates the economic claim (Zijin Gold International 15% listed minority, Zangge Mining ~75% minority, Julong 42%, Chifeng Gold ~74% minority on consolidation), so the NCI share of profit is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax-plus-leakage rate: 1 - (1 - 21% income tax) x (1 - NCI share), with NCI share stepping 20% -> 24% as Zangge/Chifeng/ZGI minorities grow. Calibration: FY2025 core EBIT RMB75.7bn x (1-0.21) x (1-0.187) = RMB48.6bn, plus the parent's 80% share of associates' profit (5.4bn), FV gains (2.9bn), net interest (-1.3bn) and non-operating items (-1.4bn) = ~RMB53.2bn vs reported attributable RMB51.8bn -- ties within 3%. NCI stock is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'; adaptations file read for currency, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule and risk-charged-once). Zijin is a diversified copper/gold/zinc/lithium miner -- an operating company with a genuine FCF stream, not a bank/REIT/holdco. FY0 = FY2025 (audited; revenue RMB349.1bn, reported FCF RMB44.4bn = OCF 75.4bn less capex 31.0bn). EBITDA is CORE: operating profit less investment income (incl. RMB5.4bn share of associates/JV profit, chiefly Kamoa-Kakula) less fair-value gains, plus finance costs and impairments, plus D&A -- FY2024 18.7%, FY2025 26.3%, H1 FY2026 35.3% of revenue. The equity-accounted JVs are instead carried in the equity bridge at book (matching-asset rule). MID-CYCLE FRAMING: H1 FY2026 margins reflect gold +53%, silver +139% and copper +38% YoY average prices -- a peak-cycle base. The base case lets FY2026 print near the current run-rate and then walks the margin down to a 23.5% mid-cycle level by year 6 (between FY2024's 18.7% at gold ~US$2,400/copper ~US$9,200 and FY2025's 26.3%), with volume growth from the 2026-2028 plan (copper 1.09 -> 1.5-1.6mt, gold 90 -> 130-140t, LCE 25 -> 270-320kt) offsetting price normalisation in the revenue line. Capex (% of revenue) starts at 10.5% to cover FY2025's RMB31bn organic capex plus the RMB15bn/yr acquisition pace (Chifeng Gold RMB18.3bn closes H2 2026) and tapers to 8%. Working capital is a 5% drag on revenue growth (receivables + inventory > payables; FY2025 OCF ran RMB4.5bn below NP + D&A). Terminal cap 12x owner FCF (cyclical). SBC is 0.07% of revenue, so house and street bases nearly coincide.
inputs.fy0_calibration: FY2025 core EBIT RMB75,716m = operating profit 82,110 - investment income 5,977 - FV gains 2,944 + finance costs 2,083 + impairments 427 + disposal loss 16. D&A 16,156 (fixed assets 12,212 + ROU 212 + intangibles 3,732) = 4.6% of revenue. Core EBITDA 91,872 = 26.3%.

equity_bridge.item: Long-term equity investments (associates/JVs incl. Kamoa-Kakula) at book
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 balance sheet line 15; their RMB5.4bn/yr share of profit is excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule). Book is well below market for Kamoa-Kakula, so this is conservative.

equity_bridge.item: Other equity instrument investments at fair value
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 balance sheet line 16 (listed stakes incl. Ivanhoe Mines / Allied Gold placement); dividend income from these is outside the core EBITDA build.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case average revenue growth over the first five forecast years (15/5/4/3/3); the equity and EPS CAGRs are rejected as a forward proxy because they compound a 2021-2025 gold/copper price upcycle rather than volume
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 26.8% vs revenue 15.3% (+75% divergence) and EPS 50.8% -- margin expansion from the metal-price cycle, not organic volume; a mid-cycle margin is used instead of extrapolating the trend
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (FY2020 RMB382m -> FY2025 RMB44,221m; FY2022 RMB3,687m -> 44,221m) are arithmetically huge and economically meaningless: the FY2020/FY2022 bases were depressed by the Julong/Kamoa build-out capex. SBC is ~0.07% of revenue, so owner and reported FCF series are indistinguishable. CAGRs computed on FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) from the Metrics CSV.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +15% (H1 +15.8%) with a 33% core EBITDA margin (H1 35.3%, H2 softer as gold retraced from ~US$5,500 to below US$4,000). Metal prices then normalise over four years toward a mid-cycle regime (gold ~US$3,200-3,500, copper ~US$9,500-10,000) while the 2026-28 volume plan (copper +40%, gold +50%, lithium 10x) and lower-cost new ounces hold revenue growth at 3-5% and settle the margin at 23.5% -- above FY2024's 18.7% because of mix and volume, below FY2025's 26.3%. Capex 10.5% of revenue falling to 8% as the Julong-3/Manono/Shapinggou/Serbia builds and the Chifeng/Zangge acquisition pace roll off. Combined tax + NCI leakage rises from 36.8% to 40% as listed-subsidiary minorities grow.

bull.narrative: The regime shift sticks: gold holds US$4,000-5,000 on central-bank reserve diversification and copper stays above US$12,000 on AI/grid demand and supply underinvestment (the Goldman/Jefferies HK$49-51 world). Kamoa-Kakula dewatering completes on plan, Julong phase 3 and Chifeng Gold deliver the 2028 volume targets, lithium reaches 270-320kt LCE into a recovered price. Revenue compounds 18/10/8/6% and the core margin settles at 28% -- still below the H1 FY2026 peak. Same capex and leakage as base; same 9% WACC.

bear.narrative: A classic cycle reversal from a record base: gold mean-reverts to ~US$2,800 and copper to ~US$8,500 by 2028 as real rates stay high and the USD firms; silver gives back most of its +139%. H2 FY2026 already weakens (FY2026 +10%), then revenue falls 8%/6%/2% as price declines swamp volume growth. Kamoa-Kakula recovery slips and resource nationalism (Congo-style concentrate export bans, Serbian suspensions) takes a tonne-and-a-half out of the copper plan; Chifeng Gold is consolidated at the top of the gold cycle. Core margin falls below FY2024's 18.7% to 17% because the new ounces are higher-cost at lower prices. Capex stays 11% of revenue for two years because the builds are committed, then is cut. Not a solvency case -- debt/assets is below 50% -- but a long derating.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation: metal prices retrace from the 2025-26 record regime over four years while the 2026-28 volume plan (copper 1.09 -> 1.5-1.6mt, gold 90 -> 130-140t, LCE 25 -> 270-320kt) and lower-cost new mines hold revenue growth positive and settle the core EBITDA margin at 23.5%, between FY2024 (18.7%) and FY2025 (26.3%). Heavy capex and acquisition spend taper from 10.5% to 8% of revenue; NCI leakage rises as the listed subsidiaries' minorities grow.
scenario_narratives.bull: Prices hold the new regime (gold US$4,000-5,000, copper >US$12,000), Kamoa-Kakula and Julong-3 deliver, lithium ramps into a recovered price; margin settles at 28% on 18/10/8% early growth. This is the sell-side world (HK$49-51 targets) with the margin still held below the H1 FY2026 peak.
scenario_narratives.bear: Cycle reversal: gold ~US$2,800, copper ~US$8,500 by 2028; revenue contracts for three years, core margin falls to 17% as the growth ounces turn out higher-cost at lower prices, DRC/Serbia jurisdiction risk crystallises in lost tonnes, and committed capex cannot be cut quickly.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear is raised to 25% because the valuation starts from a record-price base (gold +53%, silver +139%, copper +38% YoY in H1 FY2026) where a normal cycle reversal is a mainstream outcome, not a tail, and because DRC/Serbia/Congo resource-nationalism risk is live; it is not raised further because the balance sheet (debt/assets 49.6%, RMB91bn cash, long-dated CBs) carries no solvency risk. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs two independent things to hold -- the metal-price regime and flawless delivery of Kamoa-Kakula recovery plus the 2028 volume plan -- and the Kamoa flood has already shown the delivery leg can slip.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF on consolidated core EBITDA (ex equity-accounted JV income and fair-value gains), with the NCI profit share charged once as a leakage inside the tax line and equity-accounted investments carried in the bridge at book. The explicit path deliberately walks margins DOWN from the H1 FY2026 peak (35.3%) to a 23.5% mid-cycle level rather than capitalising record gold/copper prices -- the SEK.NZ peak-FCF lesson. Growth is volume-led from the disclosed 2026-28 production plan, net of price normalisation. The terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF (cyclical). The result sits well below sell-side targets because those assume the 2025-26 price regime is permanent.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold and copper prices: every 10% change in the mid-cycle margin assumption (23.5%) moves base value roughly proportionally; the model is a price-regime call

NCI leakage: Zangge Mining (~75% minority) and Chifeng Gold (~74% minority on consolidation) are consolidated 100% in revenue/EBITDA; if the leakage rate under-captures their minorities the value is overstated
Kamoa-Kakula is equity-accounted and carried at book in the bridge -- market value is materially higher, an upside the model does not credit
Capex/M&A intensity: a continued RMB15-20bn/yr acquisition pace beyond the 10.5% capex allowance would consume the modelled FCF
Jurisdiction risk (DRC, Congo export bans, Serbia, Tajikistan, PNG) is charged in the WACC premium; a large expropriation would exceed what 1.5pp prices
FX: HKD value depends on the CNY/HKD rate (1.1746 at 2026-10-22); refresh_price.py does not update fx_rate
